upstream.test: should be possible to reexport a module with unknown exports
adaptations: Select only the named a/b reexport test; omit unrelated require-of-ESM, Babel __esModule, and double-reexport tests and their imports.
Replace it/expect assertions with JSON output of the same a and b values in assertion order.
Rename e.js to e.cjs, make all import/export request extensions explicit, and add files/package.json with type module.

Keep both export-star and the side-effect import in reexport.js. Node can detect these static exports.a/exports.b assignments; this does not claim support for arbitrary computed CommonJS export names.
Preserve webpack's MIT notice in LICENSE.webpack and rspack's original THIRD-PARTY-LICENSE; see NOTES.incremental-bundler.rspack.md for verified webpack counterpart paths.

goals: Named ESM requests traverse an export-star facade to statically discoverable CommonJS exports.
Do not mistake the absence of ESM export declarations in a CommonJS dependency for an empty export surface.
